BATCH B — all seven RECOMMENDED answers chosen, each now an approved repair direction with its exact rule: D8 APPROVED-FIX — when last night's sleep is missing, recovery is UNKNOWN and no sleep restriction is applied today; every other recovery check still applies (not carry-forward of the last logged night). D10 APPROVED-FIX — date-only week counts mean 7 CALENDAR days, not 168 elapsed hours. D16 APPROVED-FIX — a 7-day forecast hit requires an eligible weigh-in on the due day or, failing that, the next day (one grace date); with no such reading the forecast is UNGRADED, not a miss; the day arithmetic follows D10. D25 APPROVED-FIX — "protein: good" requires at least one successful day within the current seven-logged-days window before the one-miss allowance applies; a first missed day cannot read "good". D32 APPROVED-FIX — "benefit replicated" counts only sessions from the CURRENT technique; all other replication thresholds stay as they are. D37 APPROVED-FIX — a merged earned receipt keeps the assessment as of the day it was earned, accepting that this can change whether a single-sighting increase counts as earned and the numbers printed on past earned receipts. D40 APPROVED-FIX — when two phones disagree on a day's calories with equal detail, ONE deterministic shared winner is chosen with the conflict kept visible and BOTH original entries retained; the exact tie-break rule and how the conflict is shown are NOT decided here and must be specified in the reviewed fix brief before anything is built. Totals: 45/45 dispositions recorded, 45 APPROVED-FIX, 0 KEEP, 0 DEFER, 0 UNRULED. What this does NOT do: it approves directions, not code — each theme still needs its accepted behaviour/delta brief, its red-first laws turning GREEN on the candidate and RED on the frozen engine, the post-fix gate's PACKAGE run and cowork's execution acceptance; the frozen app and its goldens stay untouched; no private release, spending, phone gate, remote gate or M2 closure is waived; no owner-specific interval or value is set. notes: M2-S4-REAL-DAY is S3's child under the same rule S3 was H3's, and it changes NO byte under rebuild/engine: all 20 engine files the parent pins are carried at the parent's post, byte-identical on disk, and s4-engine-files-differential measures all 45 tracked rebuild/engine files against the parent. ROUND 4 CORRECTION (DECISIONS:443): rounds 1-3 read "no engine byte moves" as "every parent carrier is carried", and the FULL refused at the first of the nineteen re-executed gates, migrate-source. The nine NATIVE-CARRIERS gates are byte-identity RECONSTRUCTIONS of rebuild/engine from a frozen BASE; four of the files they rebuild were moved by this package's ancestors (constants.cjs, writers.cjs by M2-H3-CLEAN-INIT; merge.cjs, today.cjs by M2-S3-COMPANION), so no descendant of S3 can carry them whether or not it moves an engine byte of its own - the S3 reviewer's note 3 at DECISIONS:422 named exactly this second-generation effect. This package therefore retires the same nine gates again under its OWN token line DECISIONS:444 with its OWN evidence in H3/S3's exact shape: five red-first cells, the engine-files differential over ALL 45 files, the legacy (a0-journeys) and writers (today-13) differentials it already declares, and the runner's own clean census line. The product bytes are byte-identical to the reviewed b7dc642; the r3 ACCEPT stands for the product. This package registers no D-id (DECISIONS:93, the S- slice-plan half); its obligation is the Y1 own-child rule. `notes` is not carried into the sealed artifact.

S4-REVIEW-R1 finding 4. S4 moves the runner, so EVERY package spec that pins the runner by sha has to be re-pinned or it stops at RUNNER-BYTES-NOT-THE-REVIEWED-RUNNER before any evidence is read. Round 1 re-pinned packages/S3.json and missed packages/H3.json; round 2 re-pins H3.json the same way, which is what ccf2137 did when the runner last moved and what S3 itself did to H3.json. H3.json is therefore declared role edited over the parent product pin, one byte range, tooling.runnerSha256 only.
